card.name: Bajidor Kahot
card.tagline: Modern Sundanese dance fusing Ketuk Tilu and Jaipongan
card.profile: Bajidor Kahot is a modern Sundanese created group dance from West Java which combines the dance movements of Ketuk Tilu and Jaipongan as the basis of its motions (Wikipedia). It was created around the year 2000 and is typically performed by young women in brightly colored Sundanese kebaya using fans (kipas) and scarves (selendang), shifting through dynamic formations. The dance is accompanied by Sundanese kendang drumming and gamelan, and its roots trace to the older Kliningan-Bajidoran folk performance of the Karawang and Subang regions.
card.insight: As an 'invented tradition,' Bajidor Kahot exemplifies how late-20th-century choreographers repackaged Sundanese folk vocabulary into accessible stage repertoire (Budaya-Indonesia).
